_README: Verdicts for every runtime GC-pointer holder that scripts/gc_runtime_root_holders.py
enumerates and finds NOT reached by a registered root scanner in its own file (#7231).
An entry that matches no such holder FAILS the gate. That is deliberate: it is what
makes a fix delete its own entry, and it is why 'covered_elsewhere' is a verdict rather
than a suppression — if the scanner that covers it is ever deleted, the holder stays
uncovered, the entry stays matched, and nothing tells you. Read the named scanner if you
touch it.
Verdicts:
covered_elsewhere  - a REGISTERED scanner visits it, but from a different file, so the
same-file rule cannot see it. `scanner` names it. These are the
gate's known false positives, recorded rather than silenced.
not_a_gc_pointer   - the stored value is an id, a counter, an epoch, a code address, a
.rodata object, or Rust-owned state. Nothing for the collector.
test_only          - #[cfg(test)] storage; never live in a shipped binary.
open_gap           - a real unrooted GC pointer. `issue` says where it is tracked; this
verdict FAILS while old-page relocation ships enabled.
unverified         - enumerated, verdict NOT established. This also FAILS: an unknown
movable-address contract cannot be a production exemption.
weak_pinned_old - weak canonical metadata whose old birth, movement pin and full death prune are checked by gc_keylist_invariant.py.
non_moving_snapshot - real GC addresses deliberately untraced inside one non-moving
collector window. window names start/end/owner functions and
SHA-256 source pins for the holder and reviewed control flow.
Source changes or new holder/boundary references fail the gate;
re-audit the window before updating a pin. This is a review
contract, not a static proof of arbitrary callees being safe.
#9740 extends the existing rule-T identity ratchet to raw TLS as well as Perry TLS.
The newly visible historical frontier is debt, not a safety verdict or scanner exemption.
Known census holders have explicit verdicts, including PASS1_MARKED's window contract.
weak_heap_change_cache - visible weak addresses cleared by the source-pinned heap-change funnel; never marked as roots.

holders.name: WS_PENDING_EVENTS
holders.why: The queue owns only agent/socket/server handle IDs, status codes, Rust String and Vec<u8> payloads. PendingWsEvent and WsPayload contain no JSValue or GC pointer; close callbacks remain in the separately scanned listener maps and JS values are created only after an event is removed for its owning agent.

holders.name: CAP_PHASE_CYCLES
holders.why: Cell<CapPhaseCycles> holds only nursery byte/count measurements and booleans: last/before_last come from eden_live_bytes, whole/open totals from those readings, and START resets all counts. No address, handle, JSValue or GC allocation enters any field.

holders.name: CAP_PHASE_INFLUX_BYTES
holders.why: Cell<u64> stores only capped cumulative Eden byte counts from note_cap_phase_reading and zero at start_cap_phase; no address or NaN-boxed value is stored.

holders.name: CAP_PHASE_MINORS
holders.why: Cell<u64> stores only minor-collection counts from note_cap_phase_reading and zero at start_cap_phase; no address or NaN-boxed value is stored.

holders.name: BIRTH_SHAPE
holders.why: Agent-local immutable ShapeId returned by record_birth_shape(ASYNC_GENERATOR_STATE_BRAND), which publishes the branded shape and records its external identity carrier. birth_shape writes it once. Both semantic readers (async_generator_record_of_object and generator_state::async_or_transitioned_record_bits through published_birth_shape) compare the live receiver shape to this exact identity before reading the private slot; mismatches perform the brand/property checks. No reader treats the holder alone as a semantic verdict or skips checking the receiver. It carries the shape identity, never a GC address.

holders.name: PAGE_GENERATIONS
holders.why: Address classification metadata: PageGenerationMap maps native page numbers to PageGenerationRange values (base/end addresses, generation/space enums and object_starts). object_starts points into ArenaBlock.object_starts, a Rust-owned Box<[u64]> bitmap, never a GC cell or JSValue. Ranges describe mapped arena extents and are registered/unregistered with blocks; the collector neither marks nor relocates these native metadata pointers. Const initialization makes this pre-existing holder visible to the rule-T inventory.

holders.name: COMPLETE_BIRTH_PROOFS
holders.why: #12561: cfg(test) thread-local Cell<u32> count of complete immutable birth proofs. Its only writes reset or increment the count; assertions read it to prove validated weak shape relationships do not resolve again per birth. It stores neither a heap pointer nor a NaN-boxed value and is absent from release builds.

holders.name: LINK_RESOURCES
holders.why: Per-thread numeric census of driver resources whose terminal completions still hold a link_ref. Incremented in hold, decremented in release; read only as a live-resource count. It stores neither a cell address nor a JS value; the cell refs themselves are traced and pinned by native_payload::link_ref.

holders.name: CLIENT_REQUESTS_INFLIGHT
holders.why: Set of (issuing AgentId u64, ClientRequest registry Handle i64) routing identities. mark_request inserts only Outbound.request_handle returned by perry-ffi register_handle; neither component is a GC heap address or NaN-boxed value. Request/response callbacks and actual Socket values remain in app records visited and rewritten by root_scanner::scan_http_roots. Per-agent retirement removes these scalar identities.

holders.name: TURNLOOP_UPGRADES
holders.why: turnloop P5. `HttpPendingUpgrade` carries only handle ids (i64) and an owned `Vec<u8>` of the bytes that followed the request head — no NaN-boxed value and no heap pointer. Carrying ids rather than closure addresses is deliberate: #8082 showed that a snapshot parked in a queue goes stale across a moving collection, so the dispatcher re-reads the listeners from the server handle, whose side tables scan_http_server_roots does rewrite.

holders.name: IN_FLIGHT
holders.why: InFlightRequest = three perry-ffi registry handle ids + a deadline Instant. The JS-value-bearing objects behind the ids (IncomingMessage/ServerResponse) are registered handles scanned by scan_http_server_roots via iter_handles_of_mut.

holders.name: PENDING
holders.why: Pending watcher events carry only a subscription u64 id plus Rust-owned PathBuf/String payloads and enum tags. Callback closures live in perry-ffi CallbackRoot handles, which scan_subscription_roots visits and rewrites.

holders.name: WARNED
holders.why: HashSet of perry-ffi registry handle ids already found stale, kept only to log each once. Registry ids are indices into the ffi DashMap, not heap addresses.

holders.name: CREDIT
holders.why: #9771: bytes remaining to allocate before the next native-heap sample. A `Cell<i64>` counter, const-initialised so the TLS access itself never allocates.

holders.name: UNTIL
holders.why: #9794 allocation-site sampling: bytes remaining until the next sample. A `Cell<usize>` countdown, decremented per allocation and reset on fire — a quantity, never an address.

holders.name: SEALED_YOUNG_BYTES
holders.why: Cached young-generation occupancy for the GC due check: a `Cell<SealedYoungBytes>` holding a validity flag, the heap generation it was measured at (a u64 epoch), and a byte count (Eden bytes outside the current block plus the active survivor space). Quantities only; it never stores a block, object or header address.

holders.name: DENSE_MOVE_LAYOUT_CLASSIFIED_SLOTS
holders.why: #[cfg(test)] Cell<usize> counter for asserting bounded dense-move layout classification work. It stores only a slot count and is absent from shipped binaries.

holders.name: SPLICE_COLLECT_AFTER_ROOTING_ONCE
holders.why: #[cfg(test)] Cell<bool> one-shot flag that forces a collection after splice roots its receiver and inserted values. It stores only true/false and is absent from shipped binaries.

holders.name: TEST_FORCE_RESOLVE_GC
holders.why: #[cfg(test)] AtomicUsize countdown that asks the AsyncResource resolver test to force one collection. It is a count, never an address, and is absent from shipped binaries.

holders.name: HOOK_CALLBACK_DEPTH
holders.why: Cell<usize> nesting depth for async-hook callback delivery. It stores only a counter and can never contain a GC address or JavaScript value.

holders.name: PENDING_HOOK_STATES
holders.why: Map from AsyncHook record indices to requested enabled/disabled booleans while callback delivery is nested. Both key and value are scalar state; callbacks themselves remain in HOOKS and are visited by scan_async_hooks_roots_mut.

holders.name: CRYPTO_KEY_META_REGISTRY
holders.why: Thread-local attribute table of GC_TYPE_BUFFER_CRYPTO_KEY cells: address -> numeric (algo, hash, kind, extractable, usages, bit length). The key is the address of a non-moving buffer cell, used only as a lookup key and never dereferenced through this table; the values are integers. It is consulted only after the cell's own type byte says CryptoKey (#10694), and the BufferSideTables finalize hook drops the entry when the cell is swept, so a recycled address cannot inherit it.

holders.name: FOREIGN_FINALIZER_OWNERS
holders.why: node-api-host only: addresses of foreign-backed buffer cells (non-moving, born old) that still owe a Node-API finalizer, so shutdown can release them. Used only as keys to re-find the cell for enqueue_foreign_finalizer; the finalizer record itself lives in the cell. An entry leaves when the finalizer runs, which the BufferSideTables finalize hook does when the cell is swept. Holds no edge the collector must trace: it must NOT keep the buffer alive.

holders.name: POOL_OFFSET
holders.why: Byte offset of the next free slot inside the current pool owner, a plain u32. The pool owner pointer itself (POOL_OWNER) is the rooted holder; this cell never stores a heap address. B3 routed pool placement through store_alloc, which made the file an allocating context for rule T.

holders.name: INSTALLED
holders.why: Per-thread Cell<bool> recording whether Bun realm bootstrap installed its replaceable self accessor. Only false/true are stored; the actual global and accessor closures live in the existing traced global object and descriptor storage.

holders.name: CP_LIVE_COUNT
holders.why: Atomic count of spawned children that have not reached close. It is only a lock-free emptiness gate for the reactor and root scanner; the ChildProcess values themselves live in CP_LIVE and are visited by cp_reactor_scan_roots_mut.

holders.name: CP_REFED_COUNT
holders.why: Atomic count of live child-process handles that currently keep the event loop active. It stores only a scalar count; ChildProcess JS values live in CP_LIVE and are visited by cp_reactor_scan_roots_mut.

holders.name: CAPTURED_MISS_STREAK
holders.why: Keyed by the closure's func_ptr — a CODE address, which the collector neither moves nor traces; the value is a miss-streak count.

holders.name: CLOSURE_CAP_SINGLETON_HIT
holders.why: Cache hit counter (telemetry). Holds no address.

holders.name: CLOSURE_CAP_SINGLETON_MISS
holders.why: Cache miss counter (telemetry). Holds no address.

holders.name: FUNCTION_PROTOTYPE_SLOT
holders.why: The per-agent Function.prototype OBJECT (the prototype the base Function ShapeId names), read by the shape-proven fn.bind/call/apply path. Visited by `closure::shape::scan_function_prototype_roots_mut` from the registered `object::scan_object_cache_roots_mut`, which keeps it alive and rewrites the slot when it moves. Uncovered here only because that registered scanner is in another file (same pattern as NULL_STUB_SLOT).

holders.name: VERDICT_CACHE
holders.why: Per-agent (keyed Function ShapeId u32, verdict bits u8) pairs for the Function.prototype bind/call/apply arm. Ids and flag bits, never an address; ShapeIds are never reused, so an entry can go unused but not stale.

holders.name: ACTIVE_FUNCTIONS
holders.why: Rust-owned Rc<InterpFn> AST pins and numeric root-stack indices; ASTs contain no runtime JSValues or GC heap pointers. roots_truncate releases pins on normal return and exception savepoint restoration, avoiding skipped-destructor Rc leaks.

holders.name: PIN_TOP
holders.why: Plain root-stack index (one past the newest AST pin); an integer, not an address.

holders.name: AGENT_LOOP
holders.why: turnloop P0: the calling thread's `AgentLoop` — a `turnloop::Loop` (native poller descriptor, fixed operation/handle tables, notifier and poster `Arc`s), a `turnloop::Completions` buffer, a loop id and plain `u64` statistics. P0 submits no turnloop operation, so no token, completion payload or buffer ever names a JS value; the loop only ever blocks until an `Instant` deadline or a notifier wake. Nothing stored is a GC header address or a NaN-boxed value. When P1 starts routing JS work through tokens this verdict must be re-researched.

holders.name: CLAIM
holders.why: turnloop P9: this thread's claim on its agent's route slot in `ROUTES`. `ClaimGuard` holds exactly one field, an `Arc<AtomicBool>` — the flag a wake producer reads to decide whether a parked loop needs a syscall. No JS value, no NaN-boxed word and no arena pointer ever reaches it: the guard is written only by `claim_route` (which builds the `Arc`) and read only by `claimed_flag`/`release_route`, and its `Drop` removes the matching `ROUTES` entry by `Arc::ptr_eq`. The loop itself lives in the sibling `AGENT_LOOP`, whose completions are copied out of turnloop's pooled buffers before any JS sees them (P1's rule: no heap pointer reaches the driver).

holders.name: PENDING_PATH_WRITES
holders.why: #9541: parked-write counts keyed by decoded path. `String` keys are Rust-owned heap, not GC heap, and the values are counts. No field can hold a managed pointer.

holders.name: QUEUE
holders.why: #9613: per-JS-thread Arc<EventQueue> of fs.watch RawEvents — PathBufs, EventClass tags and WatchError strings from the OS backends. Pure Rust data; no NaN-boxed values or heap object pointers ever enter the queue (events are converted to JS values only in the pump drain, under a fresh handle scope).

holders.name: SHARED
holders.why: #9613: RefCell<Option<Option<SharedInstance>>> caching the notify watcher instance (OS watcher handles + channel). Holds no JS-heap pointers; watch registrations are keyed by usize ids, targets are PathBufs.

holders.name: NEXT_READ_LINES_ID
holders.why: Monotonic id counter for READ_LINES_REGISTRY keys. The registry's own heap values are visited by scan_filehandle_roots_mut (fs/filehandle.rs:65), reached from scan_fs_handle_roots_mut.

holders.name: ARMED
holders.why: Boolean census request latch, set by census_arm and consumed at full-sweep entry; contains no address or JS value.

holders.name: LABEL
holders.why: Borrowed static Rust label (manual/signal) for the requested census, not a GC string or a NaN-boxed JS value.

holders.name: PASS1_MARKED
holders.why: Re-audited 2026-10-23 against the pinned-source diffs and current collection phases. Raw header-address snapshot exists only in a synchronous full run_to_completion: step_mark_propagation records it after tracing, then block persistence and weak/ephemeron processing only mark or clear existing edges. Full finalization skips the relocating minor prelude. step_sweep consumes the snapshot before census reporting and before reclamation; budgeted cycles and minors skip its creation and consumption. No JS callback, object relocation, or mutator window occurs between the boundaries. The added full-sweep honest-pointer verifier only reads heap slots and allocator metadata; it neither calls JS nor relocates. Scanner registration and optional feature installation occur in gc_init before this window. Trigger-watermark admission, promotion-policy estimates and test-only throw sabotage do not change the synchronous mark-to-sweep sequence; the production throw check aborts rather than calling JS or unwinding. Native Rust allocations do not collect. Removing the retired PIC census row changes reporting only. Re-audited b7f3d56fed: policy.rs adds old_gen_growth_since_last_full_bytes, a read-only query of existing pressure and post-full baseline counters for idle-reducer admission. It does not call JS, collect or relocate, and neither snapshot boundary nor the synchronous mark-to-sweep sequence changes. Re-audited DPA-R: js_gc_init_with_layouts binds immutable image metadata before runtime initialization; the compatibility wrapper and linker keepalive anchor do not touch collection, either snapshot boundary, or the synchronous mark-to-sweep sequence.

holders.name: SEQ
holders.why: u32 JSON census sequence counter, incremented once per emitted report; it never carries an object address.

holders.name: TEST_PATH_OVERRIDE
holders.why: Declared under cfg(test); holds an explicitly leaked Rust path string used by the isolated census unit tests.

holders.name: ARMED_SITE
holders.why: Cell<Option<&'static str>>: a static string-literal site NAME an armed rooting-regression test compares against, never a GC heap pointer. Declared under #[cfg(test)] only (collection_points.rs:15); the whole module compiles to an empty inline no-op outside cfg(test), so this storage never exists in a shipped binary.

holders.name: LAST_COHORT_SPLIT
holders.why: The parent copying.rs declares cohort_test_state under #[cfg(test)]; this Cell<(usize, usize, usize, usize)> holds only the byte counts of the last survivor-space/fresh-cohort split for the tenuring lock tests. It is absent from shipped binaries.

holders.name: BUDGETED
holders.why: #9794 budgeted-cycle attribution: `BudgetedCycleDiag` is counters and byte/slice tallies for the cycle in progress. No address fields.

holders.name: FULL_SITE
holders.why: #9794 trigger attribution: the `&'static str` name of the site that requested the current full collection. A pointer into rodata, not a GC allocation.

holders.name: FULL_SITE_COUNTS
holders.why: #9794 trigger attribution: per-site full-collection tallies, `Vec<(&'static str, u32)>`. Both members are rodata string literals and counts; nothing the collector traces.

holders.name: LAST_BUDGETED
holders.why: #9794: the previous budgeted cycle's four tallies as a `(u64, u64, u64, u64)`. Numbers only.

holders.name: PRIMITIVE_DISPATCH
holders.why: #9794: per-method primitive-dispatch counts, `HashMap<String, (u64, u64)>`. Rust-owned method-name strings and counters.

holders.name: THREAD_INCREMENTAL_COMPLETIONS
holders.why: #9965 verifier attribution: per-thread `Cell<u64>` tally of completed budgeted cycles. `note_incremental_completion` only increments the count and `incremental_completions_on_current_thread` only reads it; it cannot hold a heap pointer or NaN-boxed value.

holders.name: LAST_IDLE_PREDICTED_RELEASE
holders.why: #9772: releasable block BYTES the last idle selection promised — a size, not an address. A `Cell<usize>` compared against what the collection actually released.

holders.name: GC_EXTERNAL_SIDE_ALLOC_PENDING
holders.why: Byte counters for external side allocations (usize), not addresses: pending bytes noted since the last trigger check and the live external total. Nothing here can hold a GC pointer. They surfaced as rule T once regex operation scratch stopped reporting to them (#11549): the counters are no longer reached from a registered scanner's call graph, which is why the reachability walk used to cover them.

holders.name: GC_EXTERNAL_SIDE_LIVE_BYTES
holders.why: Byte counters for external side allocations (usize), not addresses: pending bytes noted since the last trigger check and the live external total. Nothing here can hold a GC pointer. They surfaced as rule T once regex operation scratch stopped reporting to them (#11549): the counters are no longer reached from a registered scanner's call graph, which is why the reachability walk used to cover them.

holders.name: GC_EXTERNAL_SIDE_DRAINED_SINCE_FULL
holders.why: External side-buffer bytes reported released since the last full baseline, including collector finalization and mutator operations such as JSON tape materialization, regex scratch teardown, native-addon adjustments and Map/Set buffer replacement. This cumulative count keeps released bytes in old-reclaim pressure until a full resets it, and can schedule a full earlier than the previous live-only term. A byte COUNT in Cell<usize>, never a heap address or NaN-boxed value. Written by gc_note_external_side_free, reset by finish_full_old_reclaim_baseline and test guards, read by external_side_old_reclaim_pressure_bytes and diagnostics.

holders.name: GC_LAST_COLLECTION_EXTERNAL_SIDE_BYTES
holders.why: Medium-parse pacing (2026-09-14): `external_side_live_bytes()` (a running sum of Map/Set entry-buffer and JSON tape side-allocation byte counts) recorded as each collection ends, read back by the parse-boundary side-allocation band to price growth since then. A byte COUNT in a `Cell<usize>`, never an address or a NaN-boxed value: written only from `note_collection_finished_arena_occupancy` and the test guard, read only by `external_side_parse_pressure_due` and `diag_tiny_parse_forced_collection`. Same shape and same verdict as its sibling `GC_TINY_PARSE_PRESSURE_BASE_BYTES` two declarations over.

holders.name: GC_OLD_RECLAIM_DEFER_BASE
holders.why: #11873: old-generation reclaim pressure in BYTES at the first allocation-point deferral, in Cell<Option<usize>>. old_reclaim_in_use_bytes sums reclaimable old-generation and external-side byte counts; defer_old_reclaim_to_precise_safepoint records that count to measure bounded growth slack. Cleared by the allocation-point valve and finish_full_old_reclaim_baseline. Neither Some nor None contains an object address or JS value.

holders.name: GC_OLD_RECLAIM_VALVE_TEST_OVERRIDE
holders.why: #11873: boolean one-shot latch in Cell<bool>, set by js_gc_old_reclaim_valve_test_override and consumed with replace(false) by defer_old_reclaim_to_precise_safepoint to force the allocation-point valve. Despite the test-oriented name, neither the declaration nor the public hidden setter is cfg(test); its researched verdict is scalar scheduling state, not test-only storage. Holds no address or NaN-boxed value.

holders.name: GC_TINY_PARSE_BOUNDARY_POLL_REMAINING
holders.why: Tiny-JSON completion countdown in a Cell<u8>. It stores only the number of bounded parse completions before the next arena-pressure poll (0..63), never an address or a NaN-boxed value.

holders.name: GC_TINY_PARSE_PRESSURE_BASE_BYTES
holders.why: #9831: `arena_in_use_bytes()` (a sum of block bump offsets) recorded as each collection ends, read back by the tiny-parse pressure guard to price growth since then. A byte COUNT, never an address or a NaN-boxed value: written only from `note_collection_finished_arena_occupancy` and the test seam, read only by `tiny_parse_pressure_due`/`diag_tiny_parse_forced_collection`. Same shape as its frontier siblings `GC_LAST_COLLECTION_POST_IN_USE_BYTES`/`GC_STEP_BYTES`, with the verdict those still owe.

holders.name: GC_YOUNG_LEAF_BORN_OLD
holders.why: #10169: a `Cell<bool>` scheduling flag — set when a document-sized JSON result was born old under young pressure, consumed by the next `gc_budgeted_due_trigger` decision. Holds no address of any kind.

holders.name: BACKOFF_SHIFT
holders.why: #10182: a `Cell<u32>` count of consecutive futile promoted-cohort fulls (capped at 3), the shift applied to the cohort bound. Holds no address.

holders.name: COHORT_FULLS
holders.why: #10182 live-subject counter: a `Cell<u64>` count of promoted-cohort fulls this thread ran. A tally, never an address.

holders.name: OLD_LIVE_AT_LAST_FULL
holders.why: #10182: a `Cell<usize>` byte count, the old-gen occupancy the last full collection verified, which the promoted-cohort bound is proportional to. Holds no address.

holders.name: PROMOTED_SINCE_FULL
holders.why: #10182: a `Cell<usize>` byte count, the bytes promoted into old-gen since the last full collection, read by the promoted-cohort bound. Holds no address.

holders.name: LAST_SURVIVAL_FOR_TESTS
holders.why: Declared under #[cfg(test)]; a `RefCell<Option<(usize, usize, usize, MinorView)>>` holding the block count, promoted and live byte counts and view verdict of the last #10241 survival probe, read by the promoted-cohort tests. Byte counts only; absent from shipped binaries.

holders.name: MINOR_REMEMBERED_PARENTS
holders.why: #10241: the remembered set of the copying minor recording for a cohort full at the same safepoint, as generation PAGE KEYS (`addr >> 12`, one `PtrHashSet<usize>` of dirty old pages), kept only for a minor that promotes in place and whose remembered set names no parent by header. Page keys are not addresses of any object and are never dereferenced; the cohort full re-derives the objects on those pages from the old page index after its own mark. Cleared by `adopt_census::begin_recording`/`discard` and consumed by `arm_survival_probe`, so it never outlives the safepoint.

holders.name: SKIP_PARENT_CHECK
holders.why: Declared under #[cfg(test)] in the survival sabotage module; a `Cell<bool>` switch. Absent from shipped binaries.

holders.name: SURVIVAL_PROBE
holders.why: #10241: the promoted-cohort full's survival probe. Holds arena BLOCK data addresses (block bases, not object pointers) as hash keys and `(start, end)` range bounds, byte counts and a view enum, plus the page keys taken from MINOR_REMEMBERED_PARENTS. Nothing is read through the block addresses: the sweep compares them with its own block snapshot and the parent check compares slot values against the ranges. Armed immediately before a synchronous non-moving full and taken immediately after it, at one safepoint with no mutator code in between.

holders.name: UNFED
holders.why: Declared under #[cfg(test)] in the survival sabotage module; a `Cell<bool>` switch. Absent from shipped binaries.

holders.name: MINOR_SEQ
holders.why: #9794: monotonic per-minor sequence number used to label survival-origin records. A `Cell<u64>`.

holders.name: FORWARDED_STUB_MEMBERSHIP_RECOVERIES
holders.why: #9717: monotonic count of array-growth forwarding stubs a budgeted full cycle admitted through `classifier_valid_object_start`, reported as `forwarded_stub_recoveries=` on the PERRY_GC_DIAG `[gc-incremental]` line. A `Cell<u64>` holding a tally, never an address — the stubs it counts are reached through the worklist, not retained here. Nothing for the collector.

holders.name: ADOPTED_BLOCKS
holders.why: #10182 live-subject counter: a `Cell<u64>` count of arena blocks whose census record the census adopted from the in-place promotion walk instead of walking them. A tally, never an address.

holders.name: BLOCK_SKIP_RECLAIMED_BLOCKS
holders.why: #10182 live-subject counter: a `Cell<u64>` count of arena blocks this thread's full sweeps reclaimed without visiting. Written only by `note_block_skip_reclaimed` with a block count; holds no address.

holders.name: BLOCK_SKIP_RECLAIMED_BYTES
holders.why: #10182 live-subject counter: a `Cell<u64>` sum of header sizes in blocks reclaimed without a visit. A byte count, never an address.

holders.name: BLOCK_SKIP_RECLAIMED_OBJECTS
holders.why: #10182 live-subject counter: a `Cell<u64>` count of objects in blocks reclaimed without a visit. An object count, never an address.

holders.name: HOLE_REBUILD_BLOCKS_SKIPPED
holders.why: #10182 live-subject counter: a `Cell<u64>` count of live old blocks a full sweep's hole-list rebuild did not parse because the census proved them hole-free. A tally, never an address.

holders.name: LAST_SKIPPED_BASES
holders.why: #[cfg(test)] `RefCell<Vec<usize>>` in `block_skip::sabotage`: the `data` base addresses of the arena BLOCKS the last full sweep skipped, recorded so tests can ask whether a given block was skipped. Block bases, not object pointers; never dereferenced, never traced, absent from shipped binaries.

holders.name: FAST_PATH_HITS
holders.why: #[cfg(test)] Cell<u64> count of fast-path answers the trigger watermark gave on this thread, so a test can assert the fast path was taken. It stores only a count and is absent from shipped binaries.

holders.name: LAST_VERIFY_BUDGETED_COMPLETIONS
holders.why: #9965 verifier attribution: per-thread `Cell<u64>` storing the preceding verifier invocation's budgeted-cycle completion count. It is compared with the current count to derive the diagnostic `after_budgeted_step` boolean and can never contain a heap pointer or NaN-boxed value.

holders.name: VERIFY_MINOR_ORDINAL
holders.why: #9965 verifier attribution: per-thread `Cell<u64>` monotonically counting evacuation-verifier invocations so failure and success diagnostics can label the minor ordinal. It stores only a saturating counter, never a heap pointer or NaN-boxed value.

holders.name: ENUM_DIAG
holders.why: #9823 for-in diagnostics (`PERRY_ENUM_DIAG`), off unless armed. Two `Instant`s and a set of u64 counters (`for_in_calls`, `for_in_primitive`, `for_in_levels`, `for_in_key_arrays`, …). No field stores an address.

holders.name: IC_DIAG
holders.why: Inline-cache miss diagnostics (`PERRY_IC_DIAG`). `IcDiag` is two `Instant`s, three counters, and `sites: HashMap<usize, SiteStat>` whose KEY is a PIC cache-slot address — malloc'd arena storage from `field_get_set/ic_slot.rs`, never GC heap — and whose value is a `String` plus counters. Nothing here is a managed pointer.

holders.name: MESSAGE_IDS
holders.why: The `messageId` promised to JS, held from submission to delivery. The VALUE is a plain `String` — no JS value, nothing for a moving collector to invalidate. That promise is minted by `js_promise_new_cross_thread()` one call earlier in the same function, so it carries the #9356/#9552 contract: pinned at creation in non-moving malloc space and rooted by its native-async token until settlement. holders.name: INTERN_TABLE
holders.why: Re-audited 2026-10-23 against the pinned-source diffs. The existing direct-mapped string-reuse cache is weak: every collection HeapChange clears all entries at entry before any free or move. gc_realloc validates the malloc cell and clears before realloc only for GC_TYPE_STRING; unrelated reallocations leave cached string addresses unchanged. Both production insertion funnels still use publish_intern_entry, which refuses publication throughout every open HeapChange, including nested scopes and realloc. Ordinary readers need no per-lookup scope check. New property-atom creation, image seeding, mixed-hash probing and weak metadata rewrite/prune operate on the separate ATOMS table; atom hits published into INTERN_TABLE still use the same guarded publication funnel. The cache itself is not scanned and holds no strong root. Const-initialized malloc bookkeeping only defers native Vec capacity reservation; it does not change string realloc validation or HeapChange ordering. Concat changes isolate numeric test counters and add no publication path. Existing tests cover unrelated/string realloc, nested publication exclusion through both writers, young-string death and live relocation.

Search objects and RegExps are held separately in RuntimeHandles; no movable address is stored in this cell.

holders.name: TEST_INLINE_DECOMMITS
holders.why: Test-only per-thread numeric count of calls to decommit_payload_pages. Pin-lifetime witnesses compare the count to detect premature OS advice even when macOS retains page contents. It stores no owner, payload address or JS value and is absent from production builds.

holders.name: TEST_PASS_CHEAP_GATES
holders.why: Test-only Boolean allowing idle-compaction prediction fixtures to pass the cheap admission gates. It stores no heap state, block address, selected object or callback; compaction state and page selection remain separate.

holders.name: PENDING
holders.why: Stable native-payload OwnerLink tokens retained with link_ref. Pinned payload cells trace and rewrite the owner back-edge and all ordinary managed state (component, Promise and primary error). Completion unrefs each link; agent retirement clears tokens before arena teardown. No JS address is retained in this queue. Moving-GC acceptance tests assert the queued operation evacuates while suspended.

holders.name: PUMPING
holders.why: Boolean reentrancy guard for the component Promise pump; contains no managed value or address.

holders.name: PENDING
holders.why: Queue of stable native-payload OwnerLink tokens, each held by link_ref until completion. Native cells are pinned; their ordinary descriptor traces and rewrites the owner back-edge, including Promise, component, server and error JS state. No JS heap addresses are stored in this queue. Normal completion unrefs; agent retirement clears plain tokens before the arena finalizes pinned cells, and TLS destruction never dereferences tokens.

holders.name: PUMPING
holders.why: Boolean reentrancy guard only. Prevents callbacks from recursively entering an active component Store through the auxiliary event pump.

holders.name: DRIVERS
holders.why: Stable native-payload OwnerLink tokens, each retained with link_ref before queue publication. Native payload cells are pinned and trace/rewrite the ordinary owner back-edge, component, invocation rows and import Promise records. Poll completion unrefs each cell; idle drivers are unpinned, and agent retirement clears tokens before arena teardown. The queue stores no movable JS value or callback frame. Public runtime acceptance tests exercise moving GC and callbacks after the public Promise is collected.

holders.name: RUNNING
holders.why: Boolean guard preventing recursive entry into the persistent driver auxiliary pump; never stores an address or JavaScript value.

_FRONTIER_README: Identity-pinned debt ratchet over new perry-ui* candidates and otherwise-unclassified core raw/Perry TLS declarations (see the census docstring, “The identity-pinned frontier”). A new uncovered holder fails until it is scanned, receives a researched holders verdict, or is deliberately pinned as debt. Moving a researched false positive to holders graduates it from this list. A fixed or classified holder makes its old frontier pin stale, so the receipt must be deleted.

frontier.name: PRIVATE_METHOD_OWNER_HINT
frontier.why: RefCell<Option<(u32, String)>>: a declaring class_id plus an OWNED Rust String naming the private method. Neither field is, or is derived from, a heap address, so a copying collection cannot invalidate it and there is nothing for a scanner to visit.

frontier.name: NEXT_SET_KEY_IDENTITY
frontier.why: Monotonic scalar key identity counter. Its tokens are stored only in owner-local ObjectMeta words and survive copying with those records; there is no address registry or scanner.

frontier.name: TEST_HASH_CALLS
frontier.why: Test-only scalar count of key hashes, used to prove evacuation performs no Set rehashing.

frontier.name: CAPTURE_DEFAULT
frontier.why: Cell<Option<CaptureSite>> contains only four u32 layout facts: the bound EventEmitter export bag ShapeId, current prototype ShapeId, data slot index and live inline count. No heap pointer or NaN-boxed value. A miss proves the native getter and ordinary symbol data descriptor; every use reloads the prototype and compares both shape stamps before loading its live value. Mutable stores are observed directly and descriptor edits invalidate the proof.
